events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20
NM...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...
Waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 445 PM EST.

* At 349 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 18 nm east of Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, moving
northwest at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, Lighthouse Point, Hillsboro Beach, Gulf
Stream, Delray Beach, Boca Raton, Highland Beach, Sea Ranch Lakes,
Briny Breezes, Pompano Beach, Deerfield Beach, Ocean Ridge, and
Fort Lauderdale.

events.region: Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 NM west of Dry Tortugas out 20 NM; Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 NM west of Dry Tortugas 20 to 60 NM out
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
For the following areas...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry Tortugas
out 60 nm...

At 345 PM EST, a possible strong waterspout was located 14 nm
southeast of Tortugas Ecological Reserve South, moving east at 10
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and large
hail.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.
Large hail could result in injury and damage to boats.

The possible strong waterspout will remain over mainly open waters.

through 433. In western Nebraska, fire weather zones 436 and 437.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.

with gusts to 50 kt this afternoon. A period of storm force
winds is expected this evening and overnight, with south winds
increasing to 40 to 50 kt with gusts of 55 to 60 kt. Steep seas

18 ft becoming very steep and hazardous.

Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize
or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.
